exEn: Tell me about your weekend!
note: Stress on the second syllable: be-RÄT-ta. berätta om = tell about. To just say something is säga.

exEn: Can I ask you something?
note: To ask for something is be om: Hon bad om hjälp. The noun is en fråga (a question).

exEn: She asked me to wait outside.
note: Irregular: ber, bad, bett. be om = ask for: be om hjälp. Jag ber om ursäkt = I apologize. Also: to pray.

exEn: She's not answering her phone.
note: svara på = answer: svara på en fråga. The noun is ett svar (an answer).

exEn: Can you explain what it means?
note: Stress on -kla-: för-KLA-ra. The noun is en förklaring (an explanation).

exEn: Can you describe the man you saw?
note: Irregular like skriva: beskrev, beskrivit. The noun is en beskrivning (a description).

exEn: Could you repeat the question, please?
note: Stress on upp-. In everyday speech people often just say: Kan du säga det igen?

exEn: Someone called out my name.
note: ropa = call out loudly to get attention; skrika = scream or yell. ropa på hjälp = shout for help.

exEn: You don't have to shout!
note: Irregular: skrek, skrikit. A baby crying loudly also skriker.

exEn: She whispered something in my ear.
What do you mean?
note: A person menar (means, intends) something; a word betyder something: Vad betyder ordet?

exEn: What does this word mean?
note: Stress on -ty-. Past betydde, supine betytt. Du betyder mycket för mig = You mean a lot to me.

exEn: I promise to call tomorrow.
note: Jag lovar! = I promise! The noun is ett löfte (a promise).

exEn: He lied to his boss.
note: lj sounds like j: "juga". Irregular: ljög, ljugit. ljuga för = lie to. Lying in bed is ligga.

exEn: I'll call you after work.
note: ringa till någon = call someone. Det ringer på dörren = Someone is ringing the doorbell.

exEn: Can you send me the pictures?
note: sk before i sounds like sj. At the table: Kan du skicka saltet? = Can you pass the salt?

exEn: What are you thinking about?
note: tänka på = think about. Jag tänker åka hem = I intend to go home. Opinions use tycka; guesses use tro.

exEn: I think she's at home.
note: For things you're not sure about: Jag tror det = I think so. tro på = believe in. Opinions use tycka.

exEn: I wonder if the store is open.
note: A polite way to ask: Jag undrar om … = I was wondering if …

exEn: I hope you're feeling better.
note: Ends in -s in every form: hoppas, hoppades, hoppats. Hoppas det! = I hope so! Not to be confused with hoppa (to jump).

exEn: Remember to buy milk!
note: The everyday word for remember. Stress on ihåg. Jag kommer inte ihåg = I don't remember.

exEn: Do you remember when we met?
note: Ends in -s: minns, mindes, mints. Like komma ihåg, but more about memories of the past.

exEn: I forgot my jacket at your place.
note: glömma bort = forget completely. Glöm det! = Forget it!

exEn: I recognized her right away.
note: Stress on igen. k before ä is soft: tj-sound. Känner du igen mig? = Do you recognize me?

ex: Jag {märkte} inte att du kom in.
exEn: I didn't notice you came in.
note: Also: to mark (with a label). Det märks = It shows / You can tell.

exEn: Guess who I ran into today!
note: g before i is soft: "jissa".

exEn: We compared prices in different stores.
note: Present is jämför (like gör, kör). jämföra med = compare with.

exEn: You get to pick the movie tonight.
note: Irregular: valde, valt. An election is ett val.

ex: Vi {bestämde} oss för att stanna hemma.
exEn: We decided to stay home.
note: bestämma sig (för) = make up your mind: Har du bestämt dig? The formal word is besluta.

exEn: We're planning a trip to Norway.
note: Verbs ending in -era are stressed on the e: pla-NE-ra.

exEn: I'll try to be on time.
note: rs merges into one sh-like sound: fö-SHÖ-ka. Försök igen! = Try again! The noun is ett försök (an attempt).

exEn: Did you manage to find the keys?
note: Ends in -s in every form: lyckas, lyckades, lyckats. Lycka till! = Good luck!

exEn: It's okay if you fail.
note: Ends in -s in every form. Failing a test is usually: Jag klarade inte provet.

exEn: He seems nice.
note: Very common: Det verkar så = It seems so. Hon verkar trött = She seems tired.

exEn: Sounds good!
note: Two meanings: to sound (Det låter kul!) and to let (Låt mig hjälpa dig). Irregular: lät, låtit.

exEn: She got angry at me.
note: Irregular: blev, blivit. Often about the future: Det blir bra = It will be fine.

exEn: We've changed our plans.
note: ändra sig = change your mind: Jag har ändrat mig. Changing trains or clothes is byta.

exEn: I'm meeting Anna on Saturday.
note: träffas = meet each other: Ska vi träffas? Trevligt att träffas! = Nice to meet you! Also: to hit (a target).

exEn: I'll meet you at the station.
note: möta = meet someone arriving or coming toward you; spending time with someone is träffa. Also: to face (a problem).

exEn: We're waiting for the bus.
note: vänta på = wait for. Vänta lite! = Wait a moment! Vi väntar barn = We're expecting a baby.

exEn: Can you show me the way?
note: visa sig = turn out: Det visade sig att han ljög = It turned out he was lying.

en: to come along; to go along
exEn: Do you want to come along to the movies?
note: Stress on med. Följ med! = Come along! följa on its own = to follow.

ex: Jag {sprang} för att hinna med bussen.
exEn: I ran to catch the bus.
note: Irregular: sprang, sprungit. False friend: the season spring is vår.

exEn: The kids are jumping into the water.
note: hoppa över = skip: Jag hoppar över frukosten. Not to be confused with hoppas (to hope).

exEn: We have to hurry!
note: sk before y sounds like sj. sig changes with the person: jag skyndar mig, vi skyndar oss. Skynda dig! = Hurry up!

exEn: We're staying home tonight.
note: Two meanings: stay, and stop moving (Bussen stannar här). To stop doing something is sluta.

exEn: Keep going straight to the roundabout.
note: Forms like sätta: fortsatte, fortsatt. Fortsätt så! = Keep it up!

exEn: We have to turn around, the road is closed.
note: vända sig om = turn around (your body). Turning left or right on the road is svänga.

exEn: The leaves fall in autumn.
note: Irregular: föll, fallit. When people fall over, Swedes usually say ramla: Hon ramlade på isen.

exEn: We moved to Sweden last year.
note: For moving home and moving things: Kan du flytta bilen? Moving your body is röra sig.

exEn: Please have a seat!
note: sätta sig = sit down (the movement); sitta = be sitting. jag sätter mig, du sätter dig.

exEn: I'm going to lie down for a while.
note: lägga sig = lie down (the movement), also go to bed; ligga = be lying. Past also written lade sig.

en: to stand up; to get up
ex: Alla {reste sig} när hon kom in.
exEn: Everyone stood up when she came in.
note: From sitting or lying. Not the same as resa (to travel). Getting out of bed is stiga upp.

exEn: Put the keys on the table.
note: lägga = put something down flat; ställa = put upright; sätta = put in place. Past la (also written lade), lagt.

exEn: Put the milk in the fridge.
note: For things that stand upright. ställa en fråga = ask a question. ställa sig = go and stand somewhere.

exEn: I put a note on the door.
note: Supine satt looks like the past of sitta. sätta på = turn on: Sätt på tv:n!

exEn: You can hang your jacket in the hall.
note: hänga med = come along, or keep up: Hänger du med? = Are you coming? / Are you following?

exEn: I pick up the kids at preschool.
note: Go and get someone or something: Kan du hämta en stol? The opposite is lämna (drop off).

exEn: I left the keys with the neighbor.
note: lämna in = hand in. Simply going away is usually gå or åka: Jag måste gå nu.

exEn: Don't forget to bring an umbrella!
note: Stress on med. Often with a reflexive: Jag tar med mig mat = I'm bringing food.

ex: Kan du hjälpa mig att {bära} väskan?
exEn: Can you help me carry the bag?
note: Irregular: bär, bar, burit. Don't confuse bär (carries) with ett bär (a berry).

exEn: She held the child by the hand.
note: Irregular: höll, hållit. hålla med = agree; hålla på med = be busy with: Vad håller du på med?

exEn: Throw me the ball!
note: Also to throw away: Kasta inte maten! Slänga means the same.

exEn: The dog caught the ball.
note: To catch a bus is hinna med bussen; to catch a cold is bli förkyld.

exEn: I dropped my phone on the floor.
note: tappa bort = lose, misplace: Jag har tappat bort nyckeln. Losing a game is förlora.

exEn: You need to pull, not push!
note: Irregular: drog, dragit. Signs on doors: DRAG = pull, TRYCK = push.

exEn: Press the green button.
note: trycka på = press (a button). Doors say TRYCK = push. Also: to print.
